name: Elienai
overview: Elienai was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Shimei. His mention in Scripture is concise, providing a genealogical link within the Benjaminite lineage. No additional details or notable events are recorded about him in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Elienai means 'my eyes [look] to YHWH,' reflecting a devotional focus toward the Lord. This meaning highlights a personal orientation of trust and dependence on God, though the name itself was not given directly by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elienai as the son of Shema, establishing his immediate paternal lineage. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Elienai's significance lies primarily in his role within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, serving as a link in the ancestral line. His mention helps preserve the heritage and continuity of God's chosen people, which is vital for understanding the broader biblical narrative of Israel's tribes. Though not a prominent figure in events or teachings, his presence in the records underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining His covenant through successive generations.
